rules.title: Short Title and Commencement
rules.description: These rules are called the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989. They came into force on 1st July 1989, except certain specified rules (Rule 9, sub-rule (3) of Rule 16, sub-rule (4) of Rule 96, sub-rule (3) of Rule 105, Rule 113, sub-rules (2)-(5) of Rule 115, Rules 118, 122, 124, 125, 126, 127) which come into force on dates notified separately by the Central Government.

amendments.description: Inserted Rule 9 reference and sub-rule (2) of rule 103

rules.title: Definitions
rules.description: Defines key terms used throughout CMVR 1989.

definitions.definition: Means the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (59 of 1988)
Any mechanically propelled 4-wheel vehicle designed to work with implements for field operations and/or trailers to transport agricultural materials. Classified as a non-transport vehicle.
Trailer generally left uncovered with single/double axle construction, coupled to an agricultural tractor by two hooks, predominantly used for transporting agricultural materials.

Rubber-tyred, rubber-padded, or steel drum wheel-mounted, self-propelled equipment (excavator, loader, backhoe, compactor, roller, dumper, grader, mobile crane, dozer, fork lift, concrete mixer, etc.) designed for off-highway operations in mining, industrial, irrigation, or construction. Non-transport vehicle; on-road driving is incidental, max speed 50 km/h.
A person or title-holder cum dealer who lets a vehicle on hire under hire-purchase, lease, or hypothecation to the operator with permission to register in the operator's name.
A Form appended to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.
Means a section of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
A certificate issued by the registering authority under Rule 35.
A motor vehicle which is not a transport vehicle.
Motor cycle with maximum design speed not exceeding 45 km/h and engine capacity not exceeding 50 cc (thermic engine).
Motor cycle with maximum design speed exceeding 45 km/h and engine capacity exceeding 50 cc (thermic engine).
Motor vehicle with at least four wheels used for carriage of passengers and their luggage.
Passenger vehicle comprising no more than 8 seats in addition to the driver's seat.
Passenger vehicle comprising more than 8 seats in addition to driver's seat, maximum mass not exceeding 5 tonnes.
Passenger vehicle comprising more than 8 seats in addition to driver's seat, maximum mass exceeding 5 tonnes.
Motor vehicle with at least four wheels used for carriage of goods.
Goods vehicle with maximum mass not exceeding 3.5 tonnes.
Goods vehicle with maximum mass exceeding 3.5 tonnes but not exceeding 12 tonnes.
Goods vehicle with maximum mass exceeding 12 tonnes.
A microprocessor chip mounted on a plastic card (ISO/IEC 7816 specification) with non-volatile rewritable memory of minimum 4 KB, used for Driving Licence and Registration Certificate applications.

A licence issued by a licensing authority in India under Chapter II of MVA 1988 to an Indian national, authorising driving of specified motor vehicle categories in countries party to the Convention on Road Traffic signed at Geneva, 19 September 1949.

A vehicle powered exclusively by an electric motor with traction energy from an onboard battery. Exempt from 'motor vehicle' classification if: (i) 30-min motor power < 0.25 kW; (ii) max speed < 25 km/h; (iii) meets pedal-assisted bicycle criteria under AIS:049:2003 and AIS:041:2003.
Single-axle agricultural machinery for soil preparation, operator walks behind it. When coupled to a trailer: max speed 22 km/h, max haulage capacity 1.5 tonnes.
Has the meaning assigned in clause (f) of section 2 of the National Capital Region Planning Board Act, 1985 (2 of 1985).

chapters.chapter_title: Licensing of Drivers of Motor Vehicles

rules.title: General — Learner's Licence Exemption During Training
rules.description: Section 3(1) of MVA 1988 (requirement to hold a driving licence) does not apply to a person receiving driving instruction, provided: (a) they hold a valid learner's licence in Form 3; (b) they are accompanied by an instructor with a valid driving licence seated in a position to control/stop the vehicle; (c) a red letter 'L' on white background (min 18 cm square, letter min 10 cm high, 2 cm thick, 9 cm wide at base) is painted/affixed front and rear.
rules.special_condition: Motorcycle learners may not carry any other person except the accompanying instructor.

rules.title: Evidence of Address and Age
rules.description: Every applicant for a driving licence must produce evidence of address and age in original or attested extracts. Acceptable documents include: Electoral Roll, Life Insurance Policy, Passport, Pay slip (Central/State/local body), School Certificate, Birth Certificate, Medical Certificate from Civil Surgeon or above. Affidavit before Executive Magistrate/First Class Judicial Magistrate/Notary Public accepted if no documents available. Foreigners must also provide proof of legal presence in India.
acceptable_documents: Medical Certificate from registered practitioner (Civil Surgeon or above)
Other documents prescribed by State Government under Section 28(k)
Proof of legal presence in India (foreigners)
rules.attest_authority: Gazetted Officer / Village Administration Officer / Municipal Corporation Councillor / Panchayat President

rules.title: Medical Certificate
rules.description: Applications for learner's licence, driving licence, addition of vehicle class, or renewal (non-transport vehicles) must be accompanied by a self-declaration of physical fitness in Form 1. Applications for transport vehicle licences must include a medical certificate in Form 1A from a registered medical practitioner (per Section 8(3) MVA). Form 1A is valid for one year from issue date and must include a passport-size photograph.
rules.form_1A: Medical certificate by registered practitioner (transport vehicles). Valid 1 year.

rules.title: Exemption from Production of Medical Certificate
rules.description: A person who has already produced a medical certificate (after commencement of these rules) for obtaining/renewing a learner's or driving licence, or for addition of a vehicle class, is not required to produce it again — except when applying for renewal of a driving licence.
rules.exception: Medical certificate IS required at time of driving licence renewal.

rules.title: Affixing Photograph to Medical Certificate
rules.description: The applicant's photograph must be affixed at the designated place in Form 1A. The registered medical practitioner must sign and seal across the photograph so that the signature and seal appear partly on the photograph and partly on the form.

rules.title: Minimum Educational Qualification for Driving Transport Vehicles
rules.description: Minimum educational qualification for a licence to drive a transport vehicle is a pass in the 8th standard. This does NOT apply to renewal of an existing transport vehicle driving licence or addition of another class of transport vehicle to a licence held before commencement of the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Rules, 2007.
exceptions: Renewal of existing transport vehicle driving licence
Addition of transport vehicle class to licence held before Amendment Rules 2007

rules.title: Educational Qualifications for Drivers of Goods Carriages Carrying Dangerous/Hazardous Goods
rules.description: From one year after commencement of CMVR (Amendment) Rules 1993, any driver of a goods carriage carrying dangerous or hazardous goods must: (a) hold a valid transport vehicle driving licence; (b) be able to read and write at least one Indian language (per Schedule VIII of the Constitution) and English; (c) hold a certificate of successfully completing a 3-day training course at a State Government-recognised institute covering Defensive Driving, Advanced Driving Skills, and Product Safety (UN classification, Hazchem Code, TREMCARD, emergency procedures). The licensing authority shall endorse the driving licence to authorise driving of goods carriages with hazardous goods.
training_topics: A. Defensive Driving — accident causes, driver fitness, vehicle condition, braking distance, highway driving, railway crossings, weather adaptation
B. Advanced Driving Skills — pre-start checklist, speed/gear/signal/lane control, overtaking, stopping, night driving (mandatory lighting, headlamp alignment, dipped beam)
C. Product Safety — UN classification, Hazchem Code, Toxicity, Flammability, TREMCARD, CIS/MSDS, Emergency Procedures (spillage, PPE, fire fighting, first aid, toxic release control)

rules.title: Application for Learner's Licence
rules.description: Application for a learner's licence must be made in Form 2 and accompanied by: (a) medical certificate in Form 1A (unless exempt under Rule 6); (b) three recent passport-size photographs; (c) appropriate fee per Rule 32; (d) for transport vehicle application, the existing driving licence; (e) proof of residence; (f) proof of age; (g) proof of citizenship.
required_documents: Form 1A medical certificate (unless exempt under Rule 6)
Existing driving licence (if applying for transport vehicle addition)

rules.title: Preliminary Test for Learner's Licence
rules.description: Every learner's licence applicant must appear before the licensing authority for a test demonstrating knowledge of: (a) traffic signs, signals, and road regulations under Section 118; (b) driver duties after an accident (death/injury/property damage); (c) precautions at unmanned railway crossings; (d) documents required while driving. Objective-type questions per Annexure VI. 'Adequate knowledge' = correctly answering at least 60% of questions. Exempt persons: holders of effective driving licence, holders of recently expired licence (within 5 years), holders of valid learner's licence, holders of certificates from notified State Government institutions.
exemptions: Holders of driving licence expired within last 5 years

rules.title: Consent of Parent or Guardian — Minor Applicant
rules.description: For a learner's licence application to drive a motorcycle without gear by a minor (under the proviso to Section 4(1) MVA), the application must be signed by the applicant's parent or guardian.

rules.title: Form of Learner's Licence
rules.description: Every learner's licence issued by the licensing authority shall be in Form 3.

rules.title: Application for Driving Licence
rules.description: Application for a driving licence must be in Form 4 and accompanied by: (a) effective learner's licence for the vehicle type; (b) appropriate fee per Rule 32; (c) three recent passport-size photographs; (d) medical certificate in Form 1A (unless exempt under Rule 6); (e) driving certificate in Form 5 from a recognised driving school (if applicable); (f) proof of residence; (g) proof of age; (h) proof of citizenship. For International Driving Permit (IDP): application in Form 4A with valid driving licence, fee, 3 passport photos, Form 1A, valid Indian national proof, passport, and visa (if applicable).
required_documents_domestic: Form 5 driving certificate from school (if applicable)

rules.title: Driving Test
rules.description: No person may appear for the driving test unless they have held a learner's licence for at least 30 days. Test is conducted by the licensing authority or an authorised person in the relevant vehicle type. The applicant must demonstrate skills covering: mirror adjustment, smooth starting, gear changing, hill starts, overtaking, signals, lane changing, emergency stopping, reversing, U-turns, response to traffic signs/lights/police signals, pedestrian crossing behaviour, maintaining left-side driving, speed regulation, use of all vehicle controls (accelerator, clutch, gears, brakes, steering, horn), road anticipation, and courteous driving.
test_skills: Smooth forward movement and gear progression
Hill start (handbrake/throttle, no roll-back), left/right turns, mirror use
Safe overtaking, allowing overtaking, meeting vehicles
Response to traffic signs, lights, police signals
Rear-view mirror use before all manoeuvres
Proper positioning at junctions (right, left, straight)
All control use (accelerator, clutch, gears, hand/foot brake, steering, horn)
Junction precautions (speed adjustment, mirror, positioning, avoidance of cutting corners, look right-left-right)
Courtesy and consideration for other road users

rules.title: Form of Driving Licence
rules.description: All driving licences issued/renewed shall be in Form 6 (standard) or Form 7 (laminated card type or Smart Card type, where apparatus is available and notified by State Government). From the date of commencement of sub-rule (3), all new and renewed licences must be in Form 7. International Driving Permits are issued in Form 6A, valid for up to 1 year or till the underlying driving licence validity, whichever is earlier. Automobile associations authorised by State/UT may issue IDPs subject to countersignature by competent authority.
rules.idp_validity: Up to 1 year or DL validity, whichever is earlier

rules.title: Addition to Driving Licence
rules.description: To add another class/description of motor vehicle to an existing driving licence, apply in Form 8 to the licensing authority with: (a) effective learner's licence and existing driving licence; (b) Form 5 driving certificate from school (for transport vehicle addition); (c) appropriate fee per Rule 32. Section 9(1), (3), and (4) of MVA apply mutatis mutandis.

rules.title: Renewal of Driving Licence
rules.description: Application for renewal to be made in Form 9 to the licensing authority having jurisdiction over the applicant's area of ordinary residence or business. Required documents: (a) appropriate fee per Rule 32; (b) three passport-size photographs (if renewal is in Form 6); (c) driving licence; (d) Form 1A medical certificate. If the DL covers both transport and other vehicles, renewal is for the appropriate period under Section 14(2) MVA. If the renewing authority is different from the issuing authority, the issuing authority must be informed. For lost/torn/mutilated licences: confirm with original authority; duplicate issued within 60 days if no response received.

rules.title: Refund of Fee on Rejection of Renewal
rules.description: Where the licensing authority rejects a renewal application under Section 15(5) of MVA, half the renewal fee is refunded to the applicant on application made within 30 days of the rejection order.

rules.title: Driving Licence for Defence Department Vehicles
rules.description: Authorities authorised under Section 18(1) of MVA to issue licences for Defence vehicles are: Army — Commanding Officers of rank Major and above; Navy — Commanding Officers of rank Lieutenant-Commander and above; Air Force — Commanding Officers of rank Squadron Leader and above.

authorities.Army: Commanding Officer, rank Major and above
authorities.Navy: Commanding Officer, rank Lieutenant-Commander and above
authorities.Air Force: Commanding Officer, rank Squadron Leader and above

rules.title: Powers of Licensing Authority to Disqualify
rules.description: Under Section 19(1)(f) MVA, the following acts by a licence holder constitute nuisance or danger to the public, enabling the licensing authority to disqualify the holder.

disqualifying_acts.act: Theft of motor vehicle
Assault on passengers
Theft of personal effects of passengers
Theft of goods in goods carriages
Transport of goods prohibited under any law
Engaging in activity likely to disturb concentration while driving a transport vehicle
Abduction of passengers
Carrying overload in goods carriages
Driving at speed exceeding the specified limit
Carrying persons in goods carriage — inside driver's cabin in excess of capacity, or on the vehicle (for hire or otherwise)
Failing to comply with Section 134 (duty after accident)
Failure to stop when signalled by an authorised person
Misbehaviour / discourtesy to passengers, intending passengers, consignors, or consignees
Smoking while driving public service vehicles
Abandoning vehicle in a public place causing inconvenience
Driving under influence of drink or drugs
Interfering with any person mounting or preparing to mount another vehicle
Allowing persons or objects to impede driver's vision or vehicle control
Not stopping a stage carriage at approved stopping places upon demand (applicable to public service vehicles)
Loitering or unduly delaying journey; not proceeding to destination per timetable or with reasonable despatch
Not driving a contract carriage to the named destination by the shortest route without reasonable cause
Driver of motor cab refusing the first offer of hire irrespective of journey length
Driver of motor cab demanding excess fare or refusing to ply
Abandoning transport vehicle as protest/agitation/strike in a public place or place causing obstruction
Using mobile phone while driving

rules.title: Endorsement by Courts
rules.description: A court convicting a licence holder for any of the listed offences must endorse (or cause endorsement of) the particulars of conviction in the driving licence.

endorseable_offences.offence: Driving without a licence or without a valid/applicable licence
Allowing licence to be used by another person
Driving while disqualified
Driving an unregistered vehicle
Driving a transport vehicle without certificate of fitness
Driving transport vehicle in contravention of permit conditions
Driving in contravention of Rule 118 CMVR
Failure to comply with Section 114 (comply with officer's directions)
Refusing/failing to produce licence or registration certificate within specified time
Failing to stop vehicle as required
Obtaining/applying for licence without disclosing existing endorsements
Driving at excessive speed
Dangerous driving
Driving under influence of drink or drugs
Driving when mentally/physically unfit
Abetment of offence under Section 183 or 186
Abetment of offence under Section 188
Unauthorised racing or trial of speed
Using vehicle in unsafe condition
Driving vehicle exceeding permissible weight/load limit
Altering a licence or using an altered licence
Offence punishable with imprisonment in which a motor vehicle was used

rules.title: State Register of Driving Licences
rules.description: Each State Government must maintain a State Register of driving licences (issued and renewed by all licensing authorities in the State) in Form 10. A printed copy must be sent to the Director (Transport Research), Ministry of Surface Transport, New Delhi.

rules.title: Driving Schools and Establishments — Licensing
rules.description: No person may establish or maintain a driving school/establishment for driving instruction for hire or reward without a licence in Form 11 granted by the licensing authority (not below rank of Regional Transport Officer). Application for grant/renewal in Form 12 or Form 13 with prescribed fee. Conditions for grant include: good character of applicant and staff, adequate premises (owned/leased, with lecture and parking facilities), sufficient financial resources, minimum one vehicle per instruction type (within 90 days of application), vehicles with dual control (except motorcycles), prescribed apparatus (blackboard, road plan board, traffic signs chart, signal charts, service chart, engine gear box, brake shoe/drums, puncture kit, tools, driving instructions manual, benches/tables, automobile mechanics books, first-aid box), instructor qualifications (10th standard pass, 5 years driving experience + motor mechanics certificate, traffic knowledge, vehicle function knowledge, English/regional language ability).

instructor_qualifications.additional_qualification: Motor mechanics certificate or higher mechanical engineering qualification from Central/State Government or BTE-recognised institution
knowledge_required: Thorough knowledge of traffic signs (Schedule to MVA)
Ability to demonstrate vehicle component functions
Adequate knowledge of English or regional language
instructor_qualifications.exemption: 5+ years instructor experience before commencement of rules exempts from language requirement

rules.title: Duration of Driving School Licence and Renewal
rules.description: A driving school licence (Form 11) is valid for 5 years. Renewal application in Form 13 must be submitted at least 60 days before expiry. Validity subject to annual certification of compliance with State Government criteria.

rules.title: Issue of Duplicate Driving School Licence
rules.description: If a Form 11 licence is lost or destroyed, the holder must immediately inform the licensing authority and apply for a duplicate. The licensing authority issues a duplicate (marked 'Duplicate') on payment of the prescribed fee. If the original is found after a duplicate is issued, it must be surrendered to the licensing authority.

rules.title: General Conditions for Driving School Licence Holders
rules.description: Holders of driving school licences must: (a) maintain annual register in Form 14 and alphabetical student list; (b) conduct training per syllabus in Rule 31; (c) issue Form 5 certificate to course-completing students; (d) submit information/returns as required by licensing authority; (e) not relocate without prior written approval; (f) keep premises and records open for inspection; (g) display school name, address, telephone on all training vehicles; (h) maintain individual trainee driving-hour record in Form 15; (i) display original licence and instructor names/addresses prominently; (j) not mislead applicants or connive to circumvent licensing provisions.

rules.title: Power to Suspend or Revoke Driving School Licence
rules.description: The licensing authority may (after opportunity of hearing) suspend for a specified period or revoke a driving school licence if the holder has: (a) failed to comply with Rule 24(3) conditions; (b) failed to maintain training vehicles in good condition; (c) failed to follow Rule 31 syllabus; or (d) violated any provision of Rule 27. Suspended/revoked licence must be surrendered to the licensing authority.

rules.title: Appeal Against Driving School Licensing Decisions
rules.description: Any person aggrieved by a licensing authority order under Rule 24(5), Rule 25, or Rule 28 may appeal within 30 days of receiving the order to the head of the Motor Vehicles Department (established under Section 213 MVA).
rules.appellate_authority: Head of Motor Vehicles Department (Section 213 MVA)

rules.title: Procedure for Appeal
rules.description: An appeal under Rule 29 must be filed in duplicate as a memorandum stating grounds of objection, with a certified copy of the impugned order and the prescribed fee. The appellate authority must pass orders within 45 days of receipt of the appeal after giving parties an opportunity to be heard.

rules.title: Syllabus for Imparting Driving Instructions
rules.description: Driving schools must follow the prescribed syllabus covering the following modules.

A_Driving_Theory_I: Know your vehicle — engine types and working

Vehicle controls — foot controls (brake, accelerator, clutch), hand controls (steering, handbrake, horn, lights, wipers, ignition, starter, indicators), other controls (mirrors, instrument cluster, windscreen)
Pre-driving checks — before and after sitting in driver's seat
Beginning to drive — precautions, moving, biting point, gear changing, stopping, braking, traffic sense, parking, positioning, reversing
Driving on road — anticipation, judgment, road positioning
Driving at intersections — MSM (Mirror-Signal-Manoeuvre) and PSL (Position-Speed-Look), zone of vision
Manoeuvres — left turn, right turn, about turn, 3-point turn, 5-point turn, U-turn, overtaking stationary and moving vehicles
Reversing — locating reverse gear, speed control, steering in reverse, S-bend weaving
Parking — parallel, angular, perpendicular, uphill, downhill
Driver responsibility — behaviour, courtesy, defensive driving, distance at railway crossings
Priority vehicles — fire engines and ambulances
B_Traffic_Education_I: Speed regulations on highways and city roads
D_Vehicle_Mechanism_and_Repairs: Fuel system (lines, injection pump, atomiser, air/oil lock)
Cooling system (radiator, water pump, fan, fan belt, overheating rectification)
Transmission — clutch, gear box, propeller shaft, differential
Brake system (hydraulic, air-assisted hydraulic, air brake, adjustment)
Electrical system (battery, dynamo/alternator, self-starter, lights, ammeter)
E_Medium_Heavy_Vehicle_Driving_Theory_II: Qualities of a good driver
Vehicle controls (major and minor)
Response of controls
Pre-driving checks
Steering (push-pull on move, gear change, turning, horn, signalling, emergency)
Gear changing (double de-clutching, single clutching, up/down shifting)
Beginning to drive in all gears including reverse and overdrive
MSM and PSL routines
Manoeuvres (passing, merging, diverging, overtaking, crossing, turning, cornering, reversing, parking)
Normal and emergency stopping, engine/exhaust brake
Stopping distance (reaction + braking)
Following distance (distance method, car length method, 2-second rule)
IPDE principle (Identification, Prediction, Decision, Execution)
Defensive driving (judgment, anticipation, escape route)
Night driving (headlight switch, dipped beam, lighting obligations)
Hill driving (uphill/downhill with parking brake and clutch slip methods)
Emergency manoeuvres (skidding, stuck horn, fire, brake failure, burst tyre, steering wobble, etc.)
Special conditions driving (wet weather, dawn/dusk/mist, dense traffic)
Towing and trailer driving
Fuel-saving methods
F_Traffic_Education_II: Road classification, design speeds, geometries, surface types, slopes
Sight distance at bends and intersections
Road junctions (T, Y, 4-arm, staggered, controlled, uncontrolled)
Traffic islands and roundabouts, channelisers, medians
Bypass, subway, overbridge, flyover driving procedures
Road markings (white/yellow lines, zebra crossings, stop lines, parking markings)
Road user characteristics (pedestrians, children, elderly, cyclists, motorcyclists, autos, buses, trucks, VIPs, emergency vehicles, animals)
Accidents (types, causes, preventive methods, driver duties)
Key provisions of MVA 1988, CMVR 1989, State Motor Vehicles Rules, Petroleum Act 1934, City Police Act, IPC 1860
G_Public_Relations: Ethical and courteous behaviour with other road users

notes: CMVR 1989 is a procedural/operational rules document. Penalty amounts and fine schedules are primarily governed by Sections 177–210 of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988, as amended by the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act 2019.
For fine calculator development, the MV (Amendment) Act 2019 schedule and State Motor Vehicles Acts must be ingested separately.
Dataset is suitable for RAG ingestion, BM25 indexing, and PageIndex retrieval for Chapters I and II of CMVR 1989.
